objective.name: bench_sims.zsh
objective.purpose: Switch-driven benchmark harness: run a chosen test scope (smoke/all/e2e/headless/single-flow) for multiple rounds across one or more iOS simulators and/or Android emulators, sequentially, then produce a comparison matrix (boot times, per-layer results, per-test speed). No-arg behavior: a default smoke run on last-ios, 2 rounds, 30s inter-sim settle.
objective.side_effects: Creates tmp/bench-<TIMESTAMP>/ (progress.log, qa-*.out, warmup-*.out). Reads back per-round tests/output/run-*/summary.json. Boots/kills devices via manage_devices.py. Invokes npm run qa (and npm run qa:flow for --flow). Runs bench_report.py for the final matrix.
invoked_languages: python3 (manage_devices.py, testctl.py, bench_report.py, inline JSON parsing)
node/tsx (npm run qa, npm run qa:flow)
path_assumptions: cd ${0:A:h}/.. sets cwd to repo root
manage_devices.py, testctl.py, bench_report.py live in scripts/
host_requirements: one or more iOS sims and/or Android emulators
ample free disk (author stress-tested on i7-9750H)

switches.effect: Smoke-tagged subset, headless+e2e layers (default scope; mutually exclusive)
Run a single flow via qa:flow; path validated to exist
Device ids/aliases per manage_devices (default last-ios); each validated up front via --kind-of to catch typos early
Idle time between sims to let host CPU calm
Abandon the whole bench after N broken-environment runs (0% pass / 0 started / no result); startup preflight not counted
Shut down ALL stray iOS sims + Android emulators first for a clean host
Print scope/sims/rounds/settle + wall-clock estimate and exit, before any preflight or device activity
Pre-confirm long runs (>= WARN_MINUTES); REQUIRED for non-interactive/detached/nohup runs

objective.required_arguments: None (minimal valid call: zsh scripts/bench_sims.zsh, uses defaults)
objective.explicit_env_checks: true (comprehensive) — broken-environment detection (per-run summary.json status), non-tty guard ([[ -t 0 ]]), load guard (sysctl vm.loadavg with LOAD_WARN/LOAD_PAUSE), and up-front --sims validation

subjective.usual_invocation: Run manually (often detached via nohup with -y) by the developer doing test-platform performance work, to compare boot/run times and pass rates across simulators and compile levels.
subjective.invocation_change_recommendation: None needed — already a clean switch-driven CLI with mutually-exclusive scopes, numeric validation, and config via env tunables. This is the house-style model the other scripts should move toward.
subjective.linux_changes_needed: Not currently portable. macOS-specific: xcrun (iOS, --prep) and sysctl vm.loadavg (load guard — Linux uses /proc/loadavg). zsh and adb exist on Linux. A Linux port would need a load-average shim and to skip/replace the iOS path; Android-only benchmarking is otherwise feasible.

macos_dependency.notes: True: xcrun (iOS + --prep) and sysctl vm.loadavg (load guard). Android-only use would still need a Linux load-average shim.

subjective.typical_runtime: Wildly variable by scope x sims x rounds. A default smoke run is tens of minutes; --all across multiple sims with several rounds can exceed 10-12 hours (e.g. --all x 4 sims x 3 rounds ~= 12.4 h).
subjective.slow_switch_warning: Yes, and it is already handled. --all and --e2e across many --sims/--rounds are inherently long (hours). The script estimates wall-clock up front, warns at >= WARN_MINUTES (default 60), prompts on /dev/tty when interactive, and REFUSES to start a long detached/non-tty run unless -y is given — a deliberate guard against accidental 12+ hour runs.
subjective.dry_run_recommendation: Already implemented (--dry-run / --plan): prints scope/sims/estimate and exits before any device activity.
subjective.destructive_steps: Boots and kills simulators/emulators via manage_devices (--warmup/--kill), --prep shuts down ALL sims/emulators, and each qa session resets the bubble_test database. Destructive to device/DB state but not to project files, and well-guarded.
subjective.rewrite_language_recommendation: Keep zsh (matches project preference and the orchestration is shell-shaped). No rewrite needed.
subjective.merge_recommendation: Keep standalone. It legitimately orchestrates manage_devices + qa + bench_report; folding it into any one of them would muddy responsibilities.
subjective.rename_recommendation: Optional — could drop .zsh for a cleaner command name, but the extension signals the shell correctly. Low priority.
subjective.relocate_recommendation: Defensible to move under scripts/bench/ alongside bench_report.py to group the benchmarking tools; otherwise fine in scripts/.
subjective.improvement_suggestions: Add a Linux load-average shim (/proc/loadavg) and an OS guard so Android-only benchmarking can run in a container. Consider persisting bench runs to a small index (it currently relies on tmp/ + reading run dirs) so historical comparisons survive tmp cleanup. testctl is not yet aware a bench is running (per memory) — emit a bench heartbeat for status visibility.
subjective.requirements_check_completeness: explicit and (near-)complete — broken-env detection, non-tty guard, load guard, and up-front sim validation; relies on the downstream qa runner's own gating for API/Metro/DB/driver health rather than re-checking them here.
subjective.external_dependency_breakdown: Scoring policy (v1.0): +1 per env var; +1 per non-standard / separately-installed program (xcrun/simctl, Android SDK tools, maestro, grpcurl, psql, gmtool, node/npm, lnav, etc.); programs shipped with macOS (ps, lsof, top, pgrep, sysctl, open, pbcopy, curl, osascript, system_profiler, git, grep/sed/awk) are NOT counted; +5 if a simulator/emulator is required on the primary path; +10 per large non-default app required (Xcode, Android Studio/SDK, Genymotion, Postgres, brew). Here: env 3 + programs 4 (python3, npm, xcrun, adb) + sim 5 (the benchmark subject) + apps 20 (Xcode 10 + Postgres 10 via qa; Android SDK +10 when benchmarking Android) = 32. (sysctl ships, not counted; down from 33.)
subjective.change_score_rationale: Weights (v1.0): Linux portability full-block +8 / partial +4 / portable 0; other dimensions +1 (or +2 where noted). Linux partial +4 (xcrun + sysctl vm.loadavg). Bench-not-visible-to-testctl + tmp-only persistence +1. No tests +1. Total 6. Already exemplary on invocation/dry-run/guards (0).
subjective.quality_score_rationale: Anchored rubric (v1.0), sub-scores sum to 100 — Error-handling/robustness /25: 22; Tests /20: 0 (no self-tests); Structure/clarity /20: 18; Documentation /15: 12; Portability + explicit requirement checks /20: 15. Total 67. Mature switch-driven CLI with a load-adaptive guard, broken-environment detection, TTY-aware long-run prompts, and an existing --dry-run; docked mainly for the macOS-bound load/iOS paths and no self-tests.
